source_observations: Trace accepts an existing torch module or dotted layer name and installs module.register_forward_hook directly on that object.
The hook can retain input/output, optionally clone/detach/retain gradients, and can return an edit_output replacement into the same forward pass.
Trace.close removes the registered hook; TraceDict composes multiple Trace hooks and removes them in reverse order.
The mechanism does not require converting the target model into a separate model class before interception.
The full package declares torchvision in addition to torch/numpy even though WP507 only needs the nethook-style mechanism.
No repository-level test or CI surface was observed in the pinned root listing; the candidate head has not moved since 2024-02-22.
hypothesis: For later WP507/J-Space model-internal matched intervention/control measurements, the highest resource-efficiency path is likely an F2-native, provenance-bound activation tap inspired by baukit's context-managed direct forward-hook pattern, rather than adopting baukit as a runtime dependency or converting the model into a separate interpretability abstraction.
counterhypothesis: Direct forward hooks may be too weak for reliable multi-token generation, shared-module/re-entrant execution, compiled runtimes, distributed models or exact cross-layer causal patching; a maintained intervention framework such as NNsight/TransformerLens/pyvene may justify its additional machinery once those requirements are measured.
